events.summary: Speaker A set the corporate strategy that the remote must be as fashionable as possible, taking ordinary products and making them user friendly and sleek.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we've got to make something as fashionable as possible, that's kind of the corporate strategy

events.summary: Speaker A said the remote is to be sold for 25 EUR, as the finance department told him.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: sell this remote for twenty five Euros

events.summary: Speaker A objected that 25 EUR is pretty dear, about forty dollars for a remote, and said it would have to do the laundry.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I'm not sold on this, it's pretty dear

events.summary: Speaker A said the profit aim is to make fifty million Euros.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: the profit aims to make fifty million Euros on it

events.summary: Speaker A proposed that the remote needs to be a universal remote control, since it will be sold internationally.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: it needs to be a universal remote control probably

events.summary: Speaker A proposed the universal remote handle NTSC, PAL and other formats, such as DVD control.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: something that could do N_T_S_C_ as well as PAL as well as various other formats

events.summary: Speaker A said the team wants to make the remote for 12.50 EUR.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we wanna try to make it for twelve fifty

events.summary: Speaker A said the team wants to make a hundred percent profit on the remote if possible.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we wanna try to make a hundred percent profit on it

events.summary: Speaker C proposed selling the remote as a remote control phone for 25 pounds or less.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: can we sell a remote control phone for twenty five pounds or less

events.summary: Speaker A said a full mobile phone may be possible, or otherwise a remote with another useful function.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: maybe a remote that has some other kind of useful function

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a remote with changeable faces, like the faces sold for phones.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Maybe a remote with changeable faces, like the faces that you can buy for phones

events.summary: Speaker D said the group has already decided the remote will be universal.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: it's gonna be universal right, we decided that already

events.summary: Speaker D objected to huge remotes with a million buttons, because you cannot tell what the buttons do.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: I've never been a fan of those huge remotes that have like a million buttons

events.summary: Speaker C proposed a PDA-style touch screen design rather than buttons, so the remote can flip between many functions.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: so touch screen design rather than button so that you can kind of flip around all sorts of different things

events.summary: Speaker D objected that if the remote does too much, users will not be able to tell the functions apart.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: if you get it to do too much you're not gonna be able to tell them apart

events.summary: Speaker B said the remote needs one outstanding feature to set it apart from other remotes.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: Needs it needs one outstanding feature to set it apart from all the other remotes

events.summary: Speaker C reported that a friend's PDA can point at any TV, detect its specifications and control it, so multi-format control is probably possible.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: I have a friend who has a P_D_A_ that he just points at his telev

events.summary: Speaker A said they like the idea of a touch screen remote with multi-format features.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: this idea of a touch screen remote with multi-format features

events.summary: Speaker B proposed using a nice material, because universal remotes look cheap and low quality.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: making it out of a nice material would be very important

events.summary: Speaker D objected that the PDA pen adds one more thing to lose, and remotes are already easily lost.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: there's such a problem with losing them, that adding this whole like P_D_A_ pen business is only one more thing to lose

events.summary: Speaker C said they like the idea of multiple changeable faceplates.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: I like the idea of the uh multi plate

events.summary: Speaker C proposed a fuzzy faceplate for cold winter days.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: We should c we should come up with a fuzzy one as well

events.summary: Speaker B proposed a locator button on the television that makes the remote find-able.
events.speaker: B
events.quote: a like a locator device, maybe a simple button that you have on your television

events.summary: Speaker A objected that a TV locator button only works if the remote is bundled with the TV, which is not the plan.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: But if we're bundling it unless we're selling their telly with the remote

events.summary: Speaker C proposed that if the remote is bundled as a phone you can call it, and otherwise it could ring like a whistle.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: if we bundle it as a phone then you can always call it

events.summary: Speaker A proposed a small device that comes with the remote and makes the remote beep when you press it, like a cordless phone page button.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: could we not do something where like just a little lit like literally just a very small kind of thing

events.summary: Speaker A proposed thinking about material quality like the sleek surgical white look Apple uses.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I think this material quality as well like I guess what we can think about

events.summary: Speaker A objected that a 25 EUR remote is pretty expensive, so features may need to be traded off for a lower price.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: twenty five Euro remote would be pretty you know it's pretty expensive

events.summary: Speaker D objected that older users such as grandmas are used to buttons and will not adopt a new design, so the marketing audience needs care.
